curriculum.title: Covenant, Kingdom, Wisdom, and Prophets: Text, Inference, and Practice Review

core.big_idea: Responsible Bible study distinguishes textual observation, canonical synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.

core.metanarrative_position: A review of observation, synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.

claims.statement: A careful reader separates direct observation from interpretation, synthesis, inference, framework position, and application.
evidence_refs: D001 Scripture as final doctrinal authority
claims.interpretive_hinge: This curriculum method follows from the project commitment to let Scripture govern doctrine while labeling the reasoning used to move from text to conclusion.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not claim Scripture uses the curriculum’s exact evidence-label vocabulary.

claims.statement: The same passage can support a strong conclusion while still requiring honesty about which reasoning step is inferential rather than explicit.
claims.interpretive_hinge: Cycle 2 contains examples where claims depend on context and canonical synthesis rather than a single sentence stating the final doctrine.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present synthesis or inference as a direct quotation.

claims.statement: Application should follow the meaning of the text rather than replacing it with a preferred modern concern.
evidence_refs: D001 Scripture as final doctrinal authority
claims.interpretive_hinge: If Scripture is the governing authority, modern application must remain accountable to what the text actually supports.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present one prudential application as universally commanded unless the evidence requires it.

core.interpretation_skill: Locate on timeline; read immediate context; identify genre; separate observation and application

learning.foundation_objective: Responsible Bible study distinguishes textual observation, canonical synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.
learning.extension_objective: Support the big idea with evidence, label the reasoning used, and identify one faithful response without overstating the text.

discussion_questions.question: What does the passage directly say or depict?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Name one thing you can point to in the text.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Which observations carry the most interpretive weight?

discussion_questions.question: How does the big idea arise from the passage or synthesis?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Which verse or passage best supports the big idea?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: What reasoning connects the evidence to the conclusion?

discussion_questions.question: What should we avoid claiming?

discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Which claims require additional canonical, historical, or interpretive evidence?

discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Explain why the response follows from the text rather than merely sounding religious.

activities.title: Evidence Label Lab
steps: Read the designated passages and record direct observations.
Place each observation or claim into the resource categories.
Discuss which conclusions require synthesis or inference.
Write one careful application that follows from the evidence.
activities.learning_link: Makes the lesson’s interpretation skill visible and concrete.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Draw the same categories on blank paper or complete the exercise verbally.

activities.title: Observation, Interpretation, or Application?
steps: Read several statements connected to the lesson.
Classify each statement as observation, interpretation/synthesis, or application.
Return to the passage and justify each classification.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Use verbal responses instead of written cards.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for what the passage reveals and ask for wisdom to respond faithfully.
closing.take_home_line: Responsible Bible study distinguishes textual observation, canonical synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.

family.title: Covenant, Kingdom, Wisdom, and Prophets: Text, Inference, and Practice Review
family.parent_intro: Read the selected passages first, keep the discussion evidence-based, and leave room for questions.

flow.instructions: Connect this lesson to something already learned in Cycle 2.
Read selected portions of the Cycle 2 passages and name direct observations.
Restate the big idea in your own words: Responsible Bible study distinguishes textual observation, canonical synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.
Use the Evidence Label Lab verbally, on paper, or with the provided worksheet.
Name one careful response that follows from the evidence without claiming more than the text supports.

questions: What does the passage directly say?
What does it show about God, Jesus, people, or the biblical story?
What is one response we can practise this week?

interactive.title: Evidence Label Lab
interactive.instructions: Use the resource to separate evidence, meaning, and response.

family.weekly_action: Revisit one Cycle 2 passage and explain what it says, what it means, and one faithful response.
family.prayer: Thank God for what the passage reveals and ask for help to respond faithfully.
family.parent_note: Questions are welcome. Do not force disclosure, certainty, giving, public prayer, baptism, or another public religious decision.

quiz.question: What should come first in careful Bible reading?
quiz.explanation: Observe what the text says before moving to interpretation or application.

quiz.question: Which statement best fits this lesson?
options: Responsible Bible study distinguishes textual observation, canonical synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.
Every detail has only one possible modern application.
Review removes the need to read passages in context.
A local tradition should control the text.

answer.text: Responsible Bible study distinguishes textual observation, canonical synthesis, inference, local framework, and application.

quiz.explanation: The canonical matrix big idea governs this lesson.

accessibility.reading_level: Upper-primary guided reading with concrete supports
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms from the passage before using theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Offer verbal or written response options.
Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read the passage aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe where helpful.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the passage, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults rather than attempting to solve them in class.
